🔴 blocker  Vietnamese comments in 88 of the 89 non-test files of the design system and screen 24
- key: src/design-system+src/screens#vietnamese-comments
- Where: 336 comment lines with Vietnamese diacritics, 224 in 61 of 62 src/design-system files and 112 in all 27 screen 24 files (the one file without is the generated src/design-system/tokens.ts); examples src/design-system/Text.styles.ts:7-8, src/design-system/Select.styles.ts:40-46, src/screens/24-project-overview/model.ts:10-13, contract.yaml:1-3. The other 81 Vietnamese lines in scope are the dictionary strings/vi.ts (legitimate). measured: python3 scan of comment lines with the brief's character class.
- Why: these comments carry the non-obvious reasons the agency must keep (why Android needs one font family per weight, fontFace.android.ts:3-6; why the Android picker sits at opacity 0.01, Select.styles.ts:43-46; why a Pressable under Link asChild needs one style object, Button.styles.ts:16-17). A developer who cannot read the reason "simplifies" the code and brings back a defect that was measured and fixed. Screen 24 is the template plan C copies: 112 Vietnamese comment lines over 27 files, so 50 screens add about 5,600 more.
- Fix: translate each comment into one English line that states the reason (most are already "why" comments, so this is translation, not rewriting); strings/vi.ts stays as it is.
- approach-changing: no, comment text plus a guard, no code changes
- trigger: an agency developer changes `opacity: 0.01` to `0` at Select.styles.ts:48 because the reason is written in Vietnamese; Android then treats the picker as invisible and TalkBack and Maestro lose the language select (the measurement recorded in that same comment)
- guard-bypass: no gate reads comment language: ESLint has no comment rule, and the dictionary audits (strings/strings.test.ts:8, e2e/web/language.spec.ts:38-46) look only at dictionary values
- design: yes, a gate that rejects the class `[a-breve a-circumflex d-stroke e-circumflex o-circumflex o-horn u-horn, the tone-marked vowels, A-breve A-circumflex D-stroke E-circumflex O-circumflex O-horn U-horn]` in comments: a local ESLint rule over `context.sourceCode.getAllComments()` for src, e2e, scripts and eslint-rules, plus one line in an existing script gate for YAML (contract.yaml has 5 such lines); string literals with diacritics allowed only in `**/strings/vi.ts` and in test data for the vi locale. The messages of the design-system text rule are Vietnamese too (eslint.config.js:90, 96; part A scope)

🟡 major  On Android, BarRow values and StatePanel sentences fall back to the system font because they skip fontFace
- key: src/design-system/BarRow.styles.ts#nativetext-skips-fontface
- Where: src/design-system/BarRow.styles.ts:21 and src/design-system/StatePanel.styles.ts:27 feed `textStyle(...)` straight to a React Native Text (BarRow.tsx:27, StatePanel.tsx:28); only Text.tsx:38 wraps it in fontFace. measured: `grep -rn "textStyle(" src` returns 3 call sites, 1 goes through fontFace.
- Why: on Android, fonts.ts:4-8 gives fontFamily "Inter"; the app registers only per-weight families "Inter-400" to "Newsreader-600" (app.json:44-119, nine families, registered under those exact names by node_modules/expo-font/plugin/build/withFontsAndroid.js:109) and src/platform/fonts.android.ts:8 loads nothing at run time. React Native checks its custom font cache, then the asset `fonts/Inter.ttf`, then calls `Typeface.create("Inter", style)` [Source: node_modules/react-native/ReactAndroid/src/main/java/com/facebook/react/common/assets/ReactFontManager.kt:65-74, 164-187], which yields the system typeface for a family the device does not know [Unverified - confirm before applying]. So the Category values ("0 / 5"), the Workload counts and the body sentence of every error panel (noAccess, notFound, unavailable, invalid) draw in the system font next to Inter: the defect class the narrow-widths work fixed for Text.
- Fix: BarRow.styles.ts:21 `export const valueText = fontFace([...textStyle('small', 'muted', undefined, true), styles.value])` and StatePanel.styles.ts:27 `export const sentenceText = fontFace([...textStyle('small', 'muted', undefined, undefined), styles.sentence])`, each file adding `import { fontFace } from './fontFace'`. Confirm on the metis-pixel emulator by comparing a screenshot of the Category values with the Inter text beside them (NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress).
- approach-changing: no, one wrapper call per site
- trigger: Android app at any width, screen 24 loaded or any error state shown: the two raw Text sites ask for family "Inter", which no Android registration provides
- guard-bypass: fontFace.android.ts applies only inside Text.tsx:38; the narrow gate measures text on web, where fonts.web.ts:4 hands over the full CSS stack; the native smoke run looks at screenshots and ids, not font families
- design: yes, the cause is a Text that accepts no width or textAlign plus a public textStyle; give Text an `align` prop and a width slot, then ban importing Text from react-native outside Text.tsx and Glyph.tsx (no-restricted-imports), so plan C cannot add a third raw Text

🟡 major  contract.yaml describes the desktop page only: on phones and in both native apps the status drill-down links are undeclared
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/contract.yaml#phone-tier-undeclared
- Where: contract.yaml:56-59 declares `status-*` as role link with a route effect; StackBar.tsx:18-23 renders those testIDs as plain Views whenever useTouchTargets() is true, which is every width of the iOS and Android apps (pointer.ts:4 `fingerOnly = true`) and web below 768 px (tier.ts:12-15, 23-26); the drill-down then lives on `legend-<status>` links (Legend.tsx:30-43) that contract.yaml never mentions. measured: `grep -c legend src/screens/24-project-overview/contract.yaml` prints 0.
- Why: contract.yaml:1 presents itself as what the screen promises, what reviewers read and what browser tests read; on the app's mobile surfaces it is false twice (status-* are not links; legend-* are controls with no declaration). The OVW-01 role check (e2e/web/controls.pages.spec.ts:76-86) and the undeclared-control check (e2e/web/controls.spec.ts:142) would both fail at phone width.
- Fix: declare `legend-*` (role link, nameFrom data, effect route 26 searchFrom drill) and record on which tier each of `status-*` and `legend-*` is a link; run the undeclared-control check inside e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts at phone width.
- approach-changing: no, the rendered behaviour is right; the contract and its gate miss a tier
- trigger: web at 390 px, or the iOS or Android app: status-done is a View with no role and legend-done is a link the contract does not know
- guard-bypass: playwright.config.ts:15-16 defines only Desktop Chrome and Desktop Safari, so every contract spec runs at desktop width where legend rows are plain text; the phone legend links are covered only by Jest tests that never read contract.yaml
- design: yes, the contract element type (e2e/web/contract.ts:16-20) has no tier field; every plan C control that changes role or moves on phones repeats this gap

The destination labels already exist in src/shell/strings/en.ts:22, 34 and src/shell/strings/vi.ts:28, 40 (`myFocus: 'Viec cua toi'`); screen 24's scope option `mine` ("My items", en.ts:15) is also `'Viec cua toi'` (vi.ts:18).
- Why: each destination name has two copies that drift when one dictionary is edited, and the vi screen already shows the clash: the sidebar entry for My focus (the fixture nav lists myFocus, src/mocks/fixtures/shell.ts:8) and the scope toggle for My items both read "Viec cua toi", and the error button "Ve Viec cua toi" reads as "back to my items".

- guard-bypass: auditDictionaries (src/screens/24-project-overview/strings/strings.test.ts:8) compares vi with en inside one dictionary; nothing compares labels across the shell and screen dictionaries

🟡 major  No guard stops a screen from hard-coding user-facing text, and model code already assembles sentences with English punctuation
- key: eslint.config.js#screens-text-guard
- Where: the ban on text written in JSX covers only `src/design-system/**/*.tsx` (eslint.config.js:80-99); screen blocks are unguarded. Seven sites in scope build text in code (measured: grep for `.join('`, a template starting with `+${` and `${label}, ` over the 89 files): model.ts:69 sign `+`, model.ts:88 `.join(', v')`, model.ts:111 `.join(' ')`, model.ts:166 `.join(', ')`, model.lists.ts:81 `.join(' ')`, Select.ios.tsx:31 and Select.android.tsx:26 `${label}, ${current}`.
- Why: in plan C a block that types `<Text variant="small">No items</Text>`, or a model that returns `'No items'`, passes every gate and ships English inside the Vietnamese UI; the joiners above put punctuation and word order in code, so a third locale (strings/index.ts:8 says "one line here") also needs code edits.
- Fix: move each joiner into the dictionaries as a template: `freshness.*` take a `{versions}` built from a `versionItem: 'v{version}'` key and a list separator key; `health.warning: '{better} {reasons}'`; `deltas.change: '+{count}'` (or Intl `signDisplay: 'exceptZero'` in core/format.ts); a field separator key for model.ts:166; a `selectName: '{label}, {value}'` key in the shell dictionary for both Select forks.
- approach-changing: no, templates replace joins
- trigger: a plan C block types a label inline; the vi page shows English
- guard-bypass: eslint.config.js:81 limits the rule to the design system; e2e/web/language.spec.ts:38-46 flags only English text equal to a leaf of the en dictionaries, so a string that never entered a dictionary is invisible to it
- design: yes, apply the selectors of eslint.config.js:88 and :94 to `src/screens/**/*.tsx` and `src/shell/**/*.tsx`, and add a check that string literals in `model*.ts` carry no letters outside the dictionaries

🟡 major  Avatar initials have two sources of truth, and the client rule gives different Vietnamese people the same initials
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/model.lists.ts#initials-source
- Where: model.lists.ts:12-18 derives initials on the client (first letter of the first two words); the shell takes them from the server (src/core/api/shell.ts:44 `user: z.object({ name: text, initials: text })`, shown at src/shell/TopBar.tsx:126). Screen 24 shows the same person through both paths: user `{ name: 'Nadia R.', initials: 'NR' }` (src/mocks/fixtures/shell.ts:31) and workload PIC `'Nadia R.'` (src/mocks/fixtures/meridian.ts:55).
- Why: Vietnamese names put the family name first and often share the middle name, so the first two words collide. measured with a python3 port of model.lists.ts:12-18: "Nguyen Thi Mai" and "Nguyen Thi Lan" both give "NT", "Tran Thi Mai" gives "TT", "Le Van Hung" gives "LV". If the server's rule for the signed-in user differs, one person carries two different avatars on one page. Screens may not import each other (eslint.config.js:160-164), so each plan C screen with a person avatar must copy initialsOf.
- Fix: carry `initials` in the overview contract's workload rows as the shell contract does (src/core/api/overview.ts:91 becomes `z.object({ name: text, initials: text, open: count, drill })`) and delete initialsOf; if the back-end cannot, move initialsOf to src/core so one rule serves every screen.
- approach-changing: no, one contract field, matching the shell contract
- trigger: a workload of Vietnamese PICs: two rows render the same "NT" avatar
- guard-bypass: the fixture PIC names are all of the "Denny K." form (src/mocks/fixtures/meridian.ts:54-57), so no screenshot or e2e shows a Vietnamese full name

🟡 major  Comments cite plan rulings, Vietnamese spec sections, wireframe line numbers and dated measurements instead of the reason
- key: src/design-system+src/screens#reference-comments
- Where: measured with python3 over the 89 files: 18 comment lines cite plan ruling ids (R-x, D-Bx, FE-x, Task N; Meter.tsx:5, Select.styles.ts:7, Text.styles.ts:7), 34 cite spec sections (status.ts:3, Legend.tsx:12, ShareBar.styles.ts:8), 78 cite wireframe line numbers (status.ts:20 `wireframe.css:199`, Banner.tsx:6 `css:266`, Card.styles.ts:6 `css:85`), 7 are dated measurement logs (`measured on 09/10/2026`: Select.android.tsx:10, Select.styles.ts:23, ProgressCard.styles.ts:11, TileRow.tsx:8), and Select.styles.ts:43 carries a tool marker `ponytail:`. 9 lines cite BRD ids (BR-32, OVW-05; model.ts:55, 110): keep those, the BRD is the agency's reference.
- Why: the ids point into Vietnamese plan files (the screen 24 plan is 919 KB) the agency will not open, so `(D-B14)` at BarTrack.tsx:6 explains nothing; line numbers into wireframes go stale at the first wireframe edit and then point at the wrong rule; a dated measurement records what someone saw, not what the code must keep.
- Fix: per comment keep one English line with the reason, for example BarTrack.tsx:6 `// The model drops zero-weight segments; draw every segment received.` and Meter.tsx:5-6 `// value is an integer percent the model already floored (99.5 shows 99).`; replace `css:NNN` with the selector name in wireframes/wireframe.css or drop it; move dated measurements into the plan; delete `ponytail:`.
- approach-changing: no, comment text only
- trigger: an agency developer reads `(renders as 600, D-B24)` at Glyph.styles.ts:26 and cannot learn why weight 700 is declared
- guard-bypass: no gate reads comments
- design: yes, the comment gate of the language finding can also reject `\b(R-[A-Z]\d+|D-B\d+|FE-\d+)\b` and `\b(css|html):\d+` in comments

🟡 major  Optional design-system props reject undefined under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, so callers duplicate JSX
- key: src/design-system#optional-props-undefined
- Where: tsconfig.json enables `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`; 18 optional props are declared `prop?: T` (Card.tsx:11, 13, 15; Button.tsx:16, 17, 19, 20; Text.tsx:13, 15, 17, 19, 20; StatePanel.tsx:10; Glyph.tsx:58; ListNote.tsx:11, 14; CountBadge.tsx:18; Select.tsx:14) and 1 as `href?: Route | undefined` (Legend.tsx:14); eslint.config.js:25 bans the conditional object spread that would otherwise forward an optional value.
- Why: a caller holding `T | undefined` cannot pass it, so it writes the element twice: StateView.tsx:76-87 repeats the whole StatePanel element to add or omit `glyph`. Every plan C block that forwards an optional model value (an href, a glyph, a testID) branches the same way, and the branches drift apart.
- Fix: declare each optional design-system prop as `prop?: T | undefined` (the Legend.tsx:14 convention); StateView.tsx:77-87 then becomes one `<StatePanel glyph={problem.kind === 'noAccess' ? 'lock' : undefined} title={problem.title} body={problem.body} actions={actions} testID={testID} />`. The `testID as string` casts at Select.tsx:29 and Select.android.tsx:32 stay, the third-party Picker type forces them.
- approach-changing: no, type annotations only
- trigger: a block passes `glyph={model.glyph}` typed `GlyphName | undefined`; tsc rejects it and the author duplicates the element
- guard-bypass: tsc forces the workaround and no gate measures duplicated JSX

💭 nit  Table view toggle reads state from the render closure
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/StatusCard.tsx#stale-toggle
- Where: StatusCard.tsx:85 `onPress={() => setTable(!table)}`

💭 nit  Unitless magic values in styles, and what no-style-literals lets through
- key: eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js#gaps
- Where: Dialog.styles.ts:12 `opacity: 0.4`, Select.styles.ts:48 `opacity: 0.01`, Logo.styles.ts:8 `aspectRatio: 248.65 / 87` (restates the wordmark SVG viewBox), StateView.styles.ts:14 `aspectRatio: 2`, Menu.styles.ts:12 `zIndex: 1`, TileRow.tsx:9 `PER_ROW = { desktop: 8, tablet: 4, phone: 2 }` tied to a one-off "773 px" measurement (TileRow.tsx:8). By reading the rule: it visits only object properties and JSX attributes (no-style-literals.js:113-126) and flags only number literals or arithmetic under sized keys (no-style-literals.js:59-66), so a number held in a const (`const PAD = 13` then `padding: PAD`), a call (`width: Math.round(tokens.gap * 1.5)`) and any string size (`width: '300px'`) all pass. measured: 0 such bypasses in the 89 files today.
- Why: the scrim opacity and the logo ratio are brand decisions with no token, so they can drift from brand/tokens.css; the rule gaps make the token gate cheap to dodge across 50 screens.
- Fix: add scrim opacity and logo ratio tokens to brand/tokens.css (generated into tokens.ts); extend the rule to report identifiers under sized keys that resolve to a numeric const in the same file, call expressions under sized keys, and strings ending in `px`.
